posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Sentinels of the Multiverse will remain in print as long as it continues to sell. But this is the last expansion. The story continues in Sentinels Tactics and possibly other games, but SotM itself was designed around a specific story arc, and GTG is determined to stay true to that vision.

It’s ending for the same reason that there isn’t an eighth Harry Potter book.

posts.name: VikenXetred
posts.cooked:
Arcanist Lupus:

It's ending for the same reason that there isn't an eighth Harry Potter book.

Except there is (in a way). Follows Harry Potter 19 years later, and is being written as a 2-part play that will also be published as a book. http://www.cnn.com/2016/02/10/entertainment/harry-potter-part-8-publish-summer-feat/

But Arcanist is right. The reason it's ending is so that it ends on a high note. The story they want to tell with the card game is drawing to a close, and they want to quit while they are ahead, rather than have a game that dies because there are 1000 decks, making it impossible to carry around. A number of users have commented that they had a game they loved that they simply stopped playing because it became ridiculous to either bring around or set up due to all the expansions it had. I think SotM pretty much nailed when to get out. There's enough to keep people entertained for hundreds if not thousands of games without issue, but not so much that they worry about how much they have to transport (esp. thanks to the case)

posts.name: adamiani
posts.cooked:
Matchstickman:

Given that during the opening days of the OblivAeon Kickstarter >G was not the top game related Kickstarter (on kicktraq) and an RPG was, I also question that assertion.

There's never been a traditional RPG kickstarter that's higher than OblivAeon is now, with 25 days left. 
(board-game/rpg hybrids Robotech RPG Tactics and Super Dungeon Explore: Legends were higher, as were some cRPGs). Not Fate, not Numenara, not Exalted or Mage. Pathfinder and D&D5 probably do better numbers but they aren't kicked. 

I love tabletop RPGs, I'm looking forward to the Sentinels Comics RPG, and I think they're very much alive and kicking as a medium. But I don't think it does anybody any good to pretend that sales haven't declined since the 80s and 90s, or that their sales are likely to be anywhere near that of the card game.

posts.cooked:
So, here's one question that's stuck with me ever since I heard Christopher (I think it was him—I can't find the post now) indicate that it's significant that Sentinels Tactics doesn't use the word "Multiverse": GTG has said all along that they have planned a fixed timeline and number of expansions for the Sentinels of the Multiverse card game, but does that mean it's the end of the card game or just the "Multiverse" card game? For example, is there plans to continue the card game past OblivAeon, but without the word "Multiverse," since it won't really exist anymore? This could be as simple as a new major storyline arc, maybe even taking place during the same time as Tactics. Or it could be a 2.0 version of the game taking place after OblivAeon with changes to the gameplay that may or may not make it incompatible with the current SOTM.

As other have pointed out, this game does seem to be the bread and butter for GTG, so I've just been wondering if they are really planning to leave it 100% behind.

I'm not really smart enough to predict one way or the other, I'm just curious.

posts.name: TheSoundOfTrees
posts.cooked:
Lohgrim:

As other have pointed out, this game does seem to be the bread and butter for GTG, so I've just been wondering if they are really planning to leave it 100% behind.

The problem, from a "story" point of view, is that, once the OblivAeon event happen, either the whole universe disappears, or alternate universes and timelines are no more accessible. And one of the prinicples of the game is that each fight we have is an "alternate timeline" one - not the fight in the story. Baron Blade only tried to pull the moon out once - and was stopped by the F5.

In other words : Sentinels of the Multiverse gameplay is based on the idea of multiple timelines/parallel universe.

Of course, another company would not hesiate to keep expanding the line - but it seems important for GtG. They prefer to expand the universe in other directions through other games. Tactics, the RPG, other projects they haven't talked about yet ( cooperative FILTER strategy game, anyone?).

However, it is always possible… I think for instance a "Golden Age" expansion for SotM, with Heroes and Villains from the past like Black Fist, old Legacy and Baron Blade's father could be compatible with the SotM line and would work well with us fans…

Anyway, they WON'T leave it "100% behind". They'll keep promoting it, will make events and challenges for it, maybe publish a few comics and books, will keep expanding through other games. And in a few years, if there is enough demand, especially from new players, work on a new edition with new art and revised gameplay. But, as a fan, I am content with the fact that they stop right where they wanted to. It's like TV shows - shows who try to outlive their story for money tend to slowly wither and lose in quality It's better to end big than slowly fade away. Time for a new adventure - that may or may not work, we will see !

RPGs tend to cost a lot less than board games, so you're comparing apples and oranges there.

I also think people's RPG-buying habits have changed. With the wealth of indie games out there nowadays I'm seeing people buying and playing lots of different products, whereas the norm 30 years ago tended to be that you'd pick a system, buy loads of books for that system and then play it pretty much exclusively. I know my RPG club is collectively buying far more this year than they did in 1995, and there are far fewer members now. And this is almost certainly because of the Internet.

The SC RPG will do just fine, especially if it doubles as a lore book.

The nice thing about an RPG is that every group's story is their own universe. There probably won't be a lot of crossover between my game and your game, but the Sentinels with be at the heart of all of them. It really is a cool way to continue the story, I think. And I think a lot of people will come to appriciate it over time like they have with the card game.

For me, the hardest part of getting anyone interested in a Sentinels game (Tactis, Card Game, or RPG) is getting them to try it. Once they play, they get hooked. Yes, it may take some time for the RPG fanbase to grow as big as the card game fanbase. But if the kickstarter is any indication, I think that there are enough fans of the game to carry it on to the next generation and beyond.

TheSoundOfTrees:

The problem, from a "story" point of view, is that, once the OblivAeon event happen, either the whole universe disappears, or alternate universes and timelines are no more accessible. And one of the prinicples of the game is that each fight we have is an "alternate timeline" one - not the fight in the story.

I'm pretty sure that's entirely unofficial, though. They've never said that's how it works, it's just what people like to think. So while I don't think they will (they've made way too big a deal of this being THE END for them to quietly launch more SotM stuff a few years down the line) there are no story reasons not to, beyond that it would be a new plot arc. The Void Guard variants attest to that, for a start.
